translations.text: Now this blessed and God-enlightened father of ours, Saint Shio, came under the guidance of the Holy Spirit and settled to the west of the capital city of Mtskheta.
And he found a very deep and harsh ravine, a wilderness without water and lacking every necessity. Its summer air was harsh, and its winter air harsher still.
And he found a small cave there and settled in it as a recluse, in hope and trust in God.
He took up this work and gave himself over to death for the sake of Him who never disregards those who trust in Him.
While this holy father of ours lived in that cave, he prayed, saying:
"O good Jesus, who came to earth for the salvation of mankind and were born of the holy Virgin, to save those who follow You and serve You with a burning heart:
now grant me also patience, so that I may complete these few days of my life in a way that pleases You. Make me worthy of Your eternal good things, through the intercession of the incorruptible
our Lady, Your Mother, Mary ever-virgin, and through the intercession of Your glorious holy apostles and of our holy father John."
He said this with tears, and through his long prayer he soaked the floor. And he made himself ready, beautifully, as a floor [?].
He persevered in prayer continually and without weariness, and God saw his eager endurance. Since nothing could be found in that wilderness to comfort the body,
that same good God who sees what is hidden, who fed Elijah in the wilderness by means of a raven,
fed this holy father of ours in the same way, for He gave him food day by day by means of a dove.
And on the right side of that cave He gave him a little water from the dry rock, which was enough for him.
When he saw such mercy of God toward him, he offered thanks to God and said:
"O Lord of glory, blessed is Your name, and great is Your mercy toward mankind. Who am I, unworthy of this mercy? Yet for everything I thank Your goodness."
And he rejoiced in spirit and glorified God. From then on he grew strong against the invisible enemies.
After he had spent a long time in that blazing furnace of solitude, providence from on high willed that this shining star should not stay hidden.
So it made him known among people, and this is how he was revealed.
At that time there was a certain prince named Evagrius. He loved Christ, was learned in the divine books, and was the son of Christians.
By the providence of God, one day he said to his sons and servants:
"Let us go out hunting." They crossed the Mtkvari (Kura) and went straight to the place where the elder was living.
Everyone scattered in different directions, and Evagrius stood alone looking around, to see if he could spot some game.
By God's permission he saw the dove that brought food to Shio.
Evagrius watched closely and saw where it went in. When they had finished hunting, they went to their homes.
The next day they went out again. And as everyone was arriving, Prince Evagrius was standing near the cave where the elder was living.
And behold, he saw that dove again, and it was bringing food for the elder.

When the blessed Evagrius watched that dove, he was astonished and followed its track. He saw the holy Shio sitting in the cave, and in amazement he said to him: "What are you, and where are you from?"
The elder said to him: "I am a stranger and a believer in Christ. I live in this small cave so that I may finish the days of my life in seclusion, and so please God without disturbance."
The blessed Evagrius said to the elder: "As the Lord lives, I will not leave you, and I will not go back to my home."
The elder said to him: "Son, you cannot bear the harshness of this desert, for I see that you were raised in great luxury."
Evagrius said: "Even if I were to die here with you this very day, I would still not leave you."
When the elder saw how firm his resolve was, he said to him: "Do what I tell you."
He replied: "I will do everything that your holiness commands me." The elder gave him his staff and said:

"Go and put this staff of mine into the Mtkvari, and it will open a way for you. Cross over on dry ground, go to your house and settle all your property, and then come back. When you reach the Mtkvari,
put my staff in again. If it opens a way for you, come to me. If it does not open a way for you, go home, for the thing you intend is not pleasing to God."
Evagrius made the elder swear an oath that he would not flee from that place.
The elder promised, and Evagrius went away. When he reached the bank of the river, he put the elder's staff in, and the water opened a way and he crossed over on dry ground.
When he had settled everything, he came back and put the staff in, and again it opened a way.
He came before the elder and said to him: "Holy father, I have done everything just as you commanded me."
The elder said to him: "My son Evagrius, know that from now on the brothers will increase in this desert. For this reason it is right that we build a church,
wherever the Lord directs us." Then they went up onto the ridge at whose foot the holy Shio lived.
When they had prayed, the holy elder took fire, poured it onto his palm, and put incense on it.
The incense smoke rose up like a pillar. Then it bent toward the western side of that ridge and settled on one spot in the gorge, standing like a pillar.
They came down. At the place the Lord had shown them, our holy father Shio struck the ground with a mattock, and they built a church to glorify God.
He clothed Evagrius in the monastic habit. News of Shio spread, and people came from all sides and became monks.
When the brothers had increased, they needed pack animals to bring in food and water.
For this reason they acquired pack animals [?]. That place was wooded and rocky, and so there were many wild beasts there.
Whenever the pack animals [?] went out to graze, the wild beasts would come out and harm them.
This grieved the brothers. Then our holy father Shio prayed to the Lord to bring those beasts before his eyes.
As he prayed, all those beasts came before the elder, and he said to them: "Why do you harm our brothers' pack animals [?]?
"Now I tell you, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who created you: go far away from these regions,
but let only one stay behind, to the glory of our God, to pasture the donkeys of our brothers."
And at that very hour they all scattered, except for a single wolf, which stood reverently before him like a servant. And he said to it:
"In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ I command you, you beast, to pasture our donkeys like a good shepherd,
so that by this you may make amends for having troubled these brothers of mine. And let your food be the same food by which we are fed.
Drive them out in the morning and bring them back at the hour of evening, and be the shepherd and guardian of our beasts."
And that wolf became obedient like a servant, and did as the elder had commanded.
Now there was one of the brothers named Conon, and his donkey fell from a cliff and died.
And the wolf brought the beasts back before the usual time, and when they counted them, Conon could not find his donkey.
He went and said to the elder: "O holy father, what have you done? You gave us a wolf as a shepherd, and look, it has eaten my donkey!"

And while he was saying this to the elder, the wolf took hold of the hem of Conon's garment and pulled him along. And the elder said to him: "Go with it, so that it may show you what has happened to your donkey."
And when they came to the top of the cliff from which it had fallen, the wolf pointed with its paw like a man, and with whimpering it vindicated itself.
And when they went down, they saw that the donkey was dead. And when Conon came back to the elder, he said to him:
"Father, this shepherd of our beasts is innocent, for my donkey fell from the cliff and is dead."
O my beloved brothers! This is how God glorifies those who fear him, so that even wild beasts submit to them like servants.
So let us also become pleasing to God through fasting, prayer, purity, mercy to the poor, love of strangers, humility,
meekness, love for one another, and every good work, which will win us the eternal good things and the delights of heaven.
Now it is fitting that we remember one of the disciples of Saint John, named Ise, renowned for every virtue: that plant of paradise, beautiful flower, and root of every good.
The holy patriarch, the Catholicos, seized this blessed Ise and consecrated him bishop for the see of Tsilkani.
He would not take this task upon himself, and falling down before the patriarch he begged to be released.
But the patriarch laid hands on him against his will and sent him to the see of the Mother of God: that Mother who raised her own mother up from error, that Mother who freed mothers from the curse,
that Mother who became mediator between God and humans and saved the whole human race, all who in faith worship Christ, the God born of her.
O all-holy Mary, Mother of God, blessed is the fruit of your womb, and blessed is the holy name of his glory,
for we were of the earth, and now through you we are served by the angels of heaven, and through you we have gained incorruption and eternal life.

For this reason it is fitting that holy men, enlightened by the Spirit, should be overseers of your temple at the see of your glory. And for this reason this worthy and holy Ise was chosen as overseer of your see, O holy Queen!
This holy father and bishop began to teach and train his flock. He went toward the north, because the people there were not yet converted and still held firmly to the worship of idols.
He began to teach them with gentle teaching. By every means, and by working miracles, he brought them to the faith: he healed the sick and drove out demons by his command.
He worked many wonders, and by teaching so well he converted many souls. He broke down the temples of the idols, built churches, baptized everyone, and strengthened them in the faith of Christ.
Adorned with such good deeds, this holy bishop Ise came back to his own episcopal see.
At that time the holy father John wished to visit his disciples and learn what measure of virtue they had reached,
and to make their good deeds known among the people, because the people were a new planting and needed strengthening.
When he arrived at that see of the holy Mother of God, he summoned our holy father Shio.

After they had greeted one another with spiritual love and sat down, the holy John, contrary to his custom, asked for a drink. Elijah the deacon brought it to him, filled a cup, and gave it to the elder.
The blessed elder said to Ise, "The bishop should be the first to pray." But Ise bowed down and asked to be excused.
Then the holy John raised the cup, prayed, and made the sign of the cross. He let go of the cup in the air, and it stood there as if on solid ground.
The One who made Peter walk on the sea as if on dry land gave the holy John the grace to do this.
After he had held the cup in the air for a long time, John said to the disciples, "Which of you will take the cup from the hand of the air?" None of them dared to reach out his hand.
Then the holy John made the sign of the cross and took the cup. All three of them [?partook of] that blessed [drink], and many others as well.
Then the holy John said to father Shio, "We should give thanks to God, who has worked this wonder among us."

The holy Shio obeyed the elder. He took burning coals and gathered them on the bare palm of his right hand. He put incense on them, and the incense gave off a fragrant smoke. He began to cense, and he censed everyone who was there.
When they saw this, they were all amazed and glorified God, who gives such grace to those who fear him.
The holy John said, "Why are you amazed, brothers? Even fire knows how to show reverence to those who know God.
This same fire recognized the three young men in Babylon, when the Chaldeans threw them into the furnace.
Dew came down from above on those who stood inside the furnace,
while those standing around it were burned, and the young men were kept unharmed. For nothing is impossible with God, and it is he who works these wonders."
Then the holy John looked at Ise and said to him, "Lord father, we wish to receive a blessing from you as well, so that we may keep it as a remembrance of you."
But he was obedient and full of the Holy Spirit, and he did not dare to disobey.
He rose, lifted up his hands and his eyes toward heaven, and prayed to God for a long time.
And then he bowed down and soaked the ground with tears, and said to the elder: "Pray for me, holy father, and follow me a little way." And holy Ise went to the river Ksani.
When those holy fathers, the lights of the world, reached the water, holy Ise began to pray.
And he raised his eyes upward together with his mind and called upon the help of God, for He does whatever He wills.
And he entreated the holy Mother of God and said with tears: "Holy Lady, may the help of the One born of you come upon me, so that this water may obey us."
And when he had prayed for a long time, he then stretched out the staff that he held in his hands and said:
"In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ I say to you, water: follow this staff of mine."
And by the grace of the Holy Spirit it at once followed those God-clothed fathers.
Now that land was barren; it was [?] as the staff was dragged along, and the water went after it,
and so he brought it to the church of the holy Lady at Tsilkani, to the glory of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
All the inhabitants of Mtskheta and of the surrounding villages saw this, and all of them glorified God.
O glorious wonder, that even the waters obey men made of earth!
One brings forth the air as a servant, and another quenches the nature of fire and drives away its heat, and another subdues water and the nature of earth.
All of them saw this and glorified God on every side.
And when holy John was leaving, his disciples also went up with him, and they stayed with him for a few days and rejoiced with him in spirit.
And when he wished to depart from there, blessed Shio entreated holy John to command him to live a life of seclusion.
And he said to him: "May your request be granted to you by God, and may He give you endurance, so that through a narrow life here you may find rest in the age to come and delight in a spacious place.
But go and first inform the patriarch, and if he commands you to live such a life, know that it is the will of God, as the apostle Paul says:
'Obey your leaders, for they keep watch over your souls.'"
And the elder taught him to confine his mind together with his body and to cast away every earthly care,
like one who is dead, buried and hidden, for this is the rule of those who live in seclusion.
And holy Shio received the commandments from the elder and kissed his feet, and all the brothers wept as at a final parting, and he said to them: "Pray for me."
And he went out, and when he entered the cathedral church, he venerated the holy Pillar and with tears prayed to God to make him worthy of serving Him in seclusion.
And he went in before the patriarch, and the patriarch received him with joy.
And when they had greeted one another, holy Shio told him everything, and also the longing of his heart.
But he sighed and wept and said to him: "Go forward, father, on that good path, and may the Lord make that cave a ladder
to lead you up to heaven, and that darkness a guide to the light that knows no night!
And may the hardship of this present time become for you eternal rest, and not for you only, but for all who will struggle in that place after you!
And stand firm against the warfare of the demons, for their warfare is full of many devices."
But holy Shio entreated him and said: "Pray for me to the Lord, that he may grant me these remaining days of mine according to his will."
And he made the sign of the cross and departed and went into his own wilderness.
And he called all the brethren together and said to them: "Behold, I have chosen the life of seclusion by the command of the elder and of the holy patriarch;
but you, beware of the snares of the devil, and acquire above all humility and obedience and meekness, which makes anger vanish, and love,
by which God is gained, and fasting, which drives away impurity, and purity of mind in prayer, which dispels all the power of the enemy,
and unceasing weeping, which brings eternal joy; and acquire poverty, so that you may find riches for eternity.
Hate the affairs of the world; train yourselves in the Scriptures, so that your mind may always be watchful;
become pure in body, so that you may become pure in spirit and enter joyfully into the wedding feast of the Lord.
Lean upon the breast of the Lord, so that you may commune with him in purity, and do not think that you will find eternal life without hardship. For Paul says
that: 'Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of heaven.' And again he says: 'By your patience gain your souls.'
"Know, my brethren, that everything here is passing away, but the eternal does not pass away.

Tell me, beloved: if a man had been in every comfort yesterday, and tomorrow had nothing left, and expected nothing else ahead except hardship and torment, would that not be a great distress for him?!"
And after much teaching he said to them: "Choose one who will take care of your life,
for I intend to settle in this cave, which I have built as a burial place for myself."
Then the brethren were grieved and wept bitterly, but he comforted them.
Then all with one accord chose the all-praised Evagrius. And he called him and said: "My son, our Lord says:
'Whoever wishes to be great among you, let him be the servant of all'; and now it is fitting for you to accept humility, which brings glory."

But holy Evagrius was meek and lowly of heart and would not take upon himself the leadership of the brethren; he pleaded the weakness of his mind and said: "I am not able to manage the service of the brethren." The elder said to him:
"If you obey me, you will receive a great reward from God and inherit eternal glory; but if you disobey me, you will be judged with the disobedient."
And he bowed down before him and said: "Whatever you command me, I will do, honoured father." And he took up the service of the brethren.
But holy Shio, dweller of the desert and beautiful flower, plant of immortality,
who brought forth good fruit with a fervent heart, in expectation of the kingdom, of eternal rest and of everlasting life, went down into the cave.
O blessed and all-blissful one, remembered with every grace, how shall I praise your courage and your wisdom? What tongue could tell of them? For you became wiser than all the wise.
For the sake of the unending light you endured this darkness of a brief moment, and in place of the passing world and its rest you received eternal glory and rest.
For Daniel was cast against his will into the den of lions, and received everlasting honour from God.
But you went down of your own will into the dark cave to fight the invisible enemy,
whom you struck down and crushed under your feet. And with that second form of baptism you sprinkled the floor, so that you might rejoice in the land of the meek.
This holy Shio lived in this way: he was afflicted in the body, but was enlightened in the spirit.
Therefore in that dark cave he delighted as if in light and rest.
Now let us speak of his teacher John.
Our blessed father John grew old in the cave and completed his course with many struggles. He grew weak and began to fail.
He summoned some of his disciples, and Tata, who lived below that mountain, and Elijah the deacon, and said to them:

"Children, the hour of my end has arrived, and I am going to my Lord. I am greatly afraid of the guardians of the air, for they are terrible; they hold back the soul so that it may not ascend to the kingdom.
You too should expect this, my beloved children. So guard yourselves now, and pray for me. And who else could deliver us from their hands
except God, who sent his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ? He set us free from death and from every diabolical passion, but only those
who follow him with a fervent heart and serve him in holiness. Therefore I beseech you that we live in holiness and righteousness."
And he commanded that his body be laid in that same place where he had lived as a stranger.
Then he received the holy mysteries and lifted up his eyes, and with a joyful face he looked upon certain ones who had come to comfort him,
and he turned his eyes toward them as toward friends, and gave up his spirit and commended it to the Lord.
Jacob's ladder was seen here too, and the angels of God were coming down.
And the Lord stood firm at the top of the ladder, and said to him: "I am the God of Abraham, your father.
Now come to me, so that I may give you rest from your labours." Thus, brothers, God glorifies those who glorify him!
His disciples wept because the holy father had parted from them.
But they disregarded the elder's word, because the place where he had directed that his body be laid seemed unworthy to them.
For priests and deacons and a multitude of people came and carried away the elder's relics, and laid them in the monastery of Tata,
…of his disciple. They made a precious reliquary, and in it they buried the holy body of our blessed father John.
His disciples wept and said: "Good father, why have you left us?
In whom will we now see the likeness of an angel? Who will heal the weaknesses of people? Who will raise up those who have fallen in mind, and who will be the medicine for those wounded by demons?
Who will water our lands with holy tears?" Weeping like this, they went away.
But holy John did not accept that his word should be disregarded. He wished his relics to be laid in the very place where he had found grace in solitude, so that we might see and believe
that even after death he is alive and has boldness before God. That is why he wished his relics to be laid there.
Severe earthquakes occurred in the place where his body had been laid, and the people of that place were struck with punishment.
Then they remembered the elder's command and understood that the earthquakes were happening because of it. So they reported it to the patriarch.
He was amazed, and he went with priests and deacons. With great honor they carried him up to his own place and laid his relics there in the same reliquary.
After that they built a church. Once he had been carried up, the earthquakes stopped.
Many other miracles also took place by the will of Christ and the grace of holy John.
Many who were sick, crippled, or possessed by demons were healed when he was carried up, and all who saw it
glorified God. Even now, if people only come to him with faith, healings take place through him.
Long afterwards, the holy Catholicos Clement built another church on the east side of that church, in the name of the holy Baptist, to the glory of the holy and consubstantial Trinity.
One of the disciples of this blessed John built Alaverdi, from which great wonders come forth to this very day.
Another built the cave of Iulta [?], and others built monasteries in Kakheti. David built the desert of Gareja and spent a long time there together with a dragon.
In the end he gave a command and drove that nest of demons out of there. He also performed many other miracles.
Another built a monastery in Zena Sopeli [?] ("the upper village") 20 [?]. No female creature can enter it, and no bird can nest there.
We cannot mention them all. Holy Ise became bishop of Tsilkani, and the tomb of that blessed man can be seen to this day.
This blessed father of ours, Shio, found the heavenly pearl in the cave and offered many souls to Christ.
He gathered a great many monks, and by his grace they are still full of every good thing, spiritual and bodily, to this day.
They delight and rejoice in spirit and glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
